title: WPSB/35/2020 of KALYAN SINGH Vs UTTARAKHAND PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 35 of 2020
Kalyan Singh ...Petitioner
Vs.
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission and others ...Respondents
Mr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Standing Counsel for the Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, learned Chief Standing Counsel assisted by Mr. C.S. Rawat,
learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel, Mr. Anil K. Bisht, learned Standing
Counsel and Mr. Suyash Pant and Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, learned Brief Holders for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Dated : 18th June, 2020
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)
The petitioner has invoked the jurisdiction of this Court
seeking a writ of certiorari to quash the order dated 22.01.2020,
disqualifying the petitioner from the selection process, as arbitrary and
illegal; a writ of mandamus directing the first respondent to permit the
petitioner to appear in the interview dated 06.02.2020 for the post of
Assistant Professor (Physics) in the Government Degree College,
Uttarakhand; and a writ of mandamus directing the third respondent-University to give the petitioner a Ph.D. certificate in Performa 2 as
sought by the first respondent.
2. The petitioner's application was rejected by the
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (for short "the
Commission") on the ground that the Ph.D. degree certificate, he had
enclosed thereto, was not in the prescribed format. On his invoking
the jurisdiction of this Court, an order was passed on 03.02.2020
permitting the petitioner to appear in the interview. Pursuant to the
said interim order, the petitioner appeared in the interview. However,
his result was kept in a sealed cover.

2
3. When the matter came up before us on 16.06.2020, we
had asked Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Standing Counsel for the
Commission, to ascertain the marks obtained by the petitioner in the
interview, and whether the petitioner had qualified therein as, in case
the petitioner did not qualify, it would be unnecessary for this Court to
examine whether rejection of his candidature by the Commission, on
the ground that the Ph.D. certificate furnished by him was not in the
prescribed format, was justified or not.
4. While contending that the Rules of the Commission
require the result, kept in a sealed cover, not to be opened, Mr. N.S.
Pundir, learned Standing Counsel for the Commission, stated that, in
case this Court so requires, the sealed cover would be opened. We
had, on the last date of hearing, pointed out that, in case the petitioner
did not succeed in the interview, the Writ Petition would be rendered
infructuous and, therefore, the sealed cover be opened.
5. Today Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Standing Counsel for the
Commission, on instructions, states that, pursuant to the directions of
this Court, the sealed cover was opened on 17.06.2020; the minimum
cut-off marks for selection and appointment to the post of Assistant
Professor (Physics) in Government Degree Colleges was 67.98 for the
general category; and the petitioner, who belongs to the general
category, had secured only 49 marks which is far below the cut-off
marks of 67.98.
6. As the petitioner had only secured 49 marks, which is far
below the cut-off marks of 67.98, it is evident that, even if his
contentions on merits are accepted, he would still not be entitled to be
appointed as an Assistant Professor (Physics) in a Government Degree
College pursuant to the selection process in which he had participated.
7. As the petitioner is not entitled to the relief of being
appointed as an Assistant Professor (Physics), in the light of the low
marks obtained by him, we see no reason to examine whether or not

3
the Commission was justified in rejecting his candidature on the
ground that the Ph.D. certificate furnished by him was not in the
prescribed format.
8. The Writ Petition fails and is, accordingly, dismissed.
No costs.
(Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
 18.06.2020 18.06.2020
Rahul
